capex_override.ack_reason: The out-of-band flag is mechanical only: the band is computed against the last FILED capex value and Annaly has never filed one under a candidate tag in the gated years (last_filed_value is null), so every value flags out-of-band, including the filing-proven $0. The figure is established by the filer's own cash-flow statements (see source), and no filed capex value exists in any gated period to anchor an estimate to.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads because Annaly, a mortgage REIT holding financial assets, buys no property or equipment and reports no capex line; the filer's own cash-flow statements fully account for investing activities in all three years, so PPE capex is $0 as a filing fact, not an estimate (same treatment as the EG/RGLD/DFTX precedents in this sweep). Measured impact is nil: the engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure — it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-12), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-6): the investing-activities section lists only payments/proceeds on securities, loans, MSR and interests in MSR, reverse repurchase agreements and JV distributions for FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 — there is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment (or any PPE capex) line in any of the three years, and the balance sheet carries no property-and-equipment line (engine ppe_net is blank for every year). The statement fully reconciles without one (dollars in thousands): FY2025 operating 692,911 + investing (27,362,734) + financing 27,219,634 = the reported net increase in cash 549,811 exactly; FY2024: 3,310,659 - 14,984,830 + 11,750,050 = reported 75,879 exactly; FY2023: 2,367,203 - 8,415,890 + 5,884,121 = reported (164,566) exactly. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 1043219 contains no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment fact in any year.

moat_against: No pricing power: Agency MBS spreads and repo funding costs are market-set; the product is a commodity financial asset
Structural leverage (GAAP 7.2x / economic 5.6x at YE2025) makes book value hostage to rate and spread moves
Persistent equity dilution: diluted share count +15.9%/yr CAGR in the engine history (ATM issuance), DPS cut in 2023 and 5-yr DPS CAGR -5.1% (fundamentals.json)
ROE is cyclical and sign-flipping (-14.6% in 2023) — no through-cycle return on capital above the cost of equity is demonstrated
moat_for: Scale and liquidity: largest U.S. mREIT, $9.4B of assets available for financing at YE2025, preferred access to repo and securitization markets
Diversified three-engine platform (Agency MBS / Residential Credit / MSR) — MSR and credit partly offset Agency spread risk across rate cycles
Internally managed (no external-manager fee drag) with a 25+ year operating history through multiple rate cycles
moat_justification: Weak: scale ($135.6B assets, largest U.S. mortgage REIT), deep repo/swap market access and a diversified three-engine platform (Agency MBS, Residential Credit, MSR) are real but replicable advantages — the assets are commodity securities anyone with financing can buy, spreads are set by the market, and there is no pricing power. Measured returns confirm no durable franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy is null for every year (no operating-income tag is filed) and gross margin is null (no revenue tag), while ROE swung from -14.6% (2023) to +7.9% (2024) to +12.6% (2025) — rate/spread-driven, not franchise-driven.
name: Annaly Capital Management, Inc.
one_liner: Diversified mortgage REIT with scale but no pricing power, moat 3/10 — on filing-direct TTM owner's earnings ($1.17/share) it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at $18.23 (weighted IRR 8.3%, weighted IV@15% $8.54; clears 15% only below ~$8.54); the 3-yr median base prints a fake Tier S off noncash mark-to-market addbacks and the company's own EAD ($2.92/share FY2025) reaches only Tier B — sector model misfit, confidence low.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine's sanity band anchors on the last FILED SBC value and Annaly has filed no ShareBasedCompensation value in any gated period (last_filed_value is null in the engine's history window), so no in-band value exists. The $28.0M is not an estimate — it is the equity-based compensation expense Annaly itself disclosed in Note 14 of its FY2025 10-K.
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every tag the engine reads; the filer's own 10-K Note 14 discloses the equity-based compensation expense for each year ($17.3M / $23.2M / $28.0M). A single override value fills every untagged year, so the latest filed year (FY2025, $28.0M) is used for all years: it overstates FY2024 and FY2023, i.e. it errs in the conservative direction (more SBC = lower owner's earnings), and the amount is immaterial either way — $28M is ~$0.04/share against a normalized OE base of several dollars per share (under ~1% of the base in each gated year).
sbc_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-12), Note 14 Long-Term Stock Incentive Plan (p. F-30): 'The Company recognized equity-based compensation expense of $28.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.' The same note in the FY2024 10-K reports $23.2 million for FY2024 and in the FY2023 10-K $17.3 million for FY2023 — EDGAR companyfacts carries no ShareBasedCompensation annual fact for 2023-2025 (the tag was last filed for FY2009), so the expense is disclosed only in this note.
